metrics.label: Hip turn at the top
metrics.blurb: how far the hips rotate at the top
metrics.why: the hips turn alongside the shoulders during the backswing; the difference between the two creates separation

metrics.label: Hip rotation at impact
metrics.blurb: how open the hips are at impact
metrics.why: the hips lead the body's rotation through the ball

metrics.label: Weight shift
metrics.blurb: how much the hips slide toward the target
metrics.why: some sideways hip drive toward the target is part of transferring weight through the ball

metrics.label: Spine angle at address
metrics.blurb: how much the upper body leans at setup
metrics.why: the spine angle at setup sets the posture the swing is built around

metrics.label: Tempo (backswing : downswing)
metrics.why: many tour swings settle near a 3-to-1 backswing-to-downswing rhythm

metrics.label: Shoulder turn
metrics.blurb: how far the shoulders rotate at the top
metrics.why: shoulder rotation is the main way the body coils to store energy for the downswing

metrics.label: X-factor (shoulder–hip separation)
metrics.blurb: the gap between shoulder turn and hip turn at the top
metrics.why: this separation is a big part of how the body stores and releases power

metrics.label: Spine angle at impact
metrics.blurb: how much the upper body leans at impact
metrics.why: keeping a similar posture from setup to impact helps the swing stay on plane

metrics.label: Posture (spine angle change)
metrics.blurb: how much the spine angle changes from setup to impact
metrics.why: tour swings tend to hold their setup posture fairly well into impact
